slowest_experiments.experiment: V632 exact Markdown and YAML task-contract preflight

summary: Two experiments completed in 0.3 minutes. The sole compute-bound entry, Qwen3.8 claim/evidence structured trace capture, took 0.01 minutes; the 0.28-minute synthesis-only preflight was the longest entry overall. The locked task-conditioned indicator is false, so no compute-bound GPU-idle fault is recorded.
bottlenecks_identified: The synthesis-only exact Markdown and YAML preflight was the longest recorded entry at 0.28 minutes and is the only observed candidate for elapsed-time reduction; GPU activity does not apply to it.
Timing observability was incomplete: milestone timing came from disk-mtime reconstruction because the live git-log path found 0 commits.
The supplied data has no task-aligned phase trace, so it does not explain the 0.01-minute compute-bound duration.
improvements_suggested: Add content-addressed caching to the exact Markdown and YAML preflight so unchanged task contracts can bypass repeated validation.
Emit monotonic start, stop, and phase timestamps for each experiment instead of depending on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Capture experiment-scoped GPU samples with process ownership during compute-bound phases.
Record model count and runner choice so DualGPURunner eligibility can be checked only when 2 or more models run in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Cache unchanged exact Markdown and YAML preflight results by content hash.
Write direct monotonic experiment and phase timing into each result artifact.
Add task-owned GPU, model-count, and runner-choice receipts for compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: This record can rank the two entries, but it cannot explain causal phase cost or task-window GPU behavior. No data available this milestone establishes a parallel multi-model task or a missed DualGPURunner dispatch. Task-scoped timing and accelerator receipts would make the next retrospective actionable without treating synthesis-only or report-snapshot GPU idle as a compute failure.
